verify.source: cognigate.dev publishes '~38ms MEDIAN TARGET' and '<120ms P99 BUDGET' as the design budget for the reference gate. The claim is stated as a TARGET, matching that language exactly — it is not represented as a measurement.

claims.note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26. Was '~8ms p50 / ~20ms p95', presented as measured fact and reconciling with nothing. Two traps were found while fixing it. First: vorion/docs/benchmarks/phase6-performance.md measures p50 12ms / p95 28ms — but that row is `GET /stats`, a dashboard read, and the fastest endpoint in the table; the policy-decision endpoint (`POST /role-gates/evaluate`) measures 18/42. Second: that file benchmarks Vorion's Phase 6 Trust Engine, not CogniGate, so citing it here would swap one mis-attribution for another. CogniGate has no measured latency artifact — the `p50` in cognigate/tests/test_monte_carlo.py is a probability variable, not latency. The honest claim is therefore CogniGate's own published design target, worded as a target. If a real CogniGate benchmark is ever produced, replace this with the measurement and drop the word 'target'.
